In this thought-provoking session, acclaimed writer Laura Spinney explores the "epic" history of Proto-Indo-European (PIE)—the ancestral tongue of nearly 3 billion people today. From the nomadic herders of the Eurasian steppe to the ancient Sanskrit texts of India, Spinney reveals how language has been shaped not by "racial purity," but by staggering mobility and survival.
She challenges the modern obsession with borders and nationalism, arguing that our shared linguistic roots prove that human history is, at its core, a story of migration.
Thank you for watching our video!
